answer: Zero-knowledge proof-of-personhood resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to prove its public key maps to an unspent nullifier from a verified human credential. Rather than using a brittle CAPTCHA relic across a noisy tundra of cloud bots, the protocol ties each key to a distinct human island, forcing attackers to recruit one real person per identity. However, credential-rental markets still let well-funded adversaries buy multiple slots.
